transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main reason I’m here is that I just can’t keep my mind on something long enough to actually finish it anymore, even when it really matters. I work in computer support, so a lot of my job is following a problem step by step, like tracing a client’s network issue through logs or settings, and I’ll start doing that and then suddenly realize ten minutes have gone by and I’ve reread the same log entries three times and I still couldn’t tell you what they said.

It’s frustrating, because it’s not that I don’t care or that the work is too hard. I know how to do it. But my mind just slips off the task, and then I have to keep dragging it back, and sometimes I’m not even aware it happened until I’ve lost a chunk of time. It’s gotten to the point where it feels like I’m fighting my own brain just to get through things that should be routine.
Thinking back, did you have similar trouble focusing and finishing tasks as a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only become a problem recently?

No, it definitely goes way back. I mean, my mother still brings it up—kind of laughing about it now, but I think it was probably pretty aggravating at the time. She says my grade school report cards were always some version of, “He’s bright, but…” and then the “but” would be that I wouldn’t stay in my seat, or I’d blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking, or I’d somehow lose homework even when I had actually done it.

And that last part is the one that still makes me wince, because I remember that happening. It wasn’t always that I didn’t do the assignment—it was that it vanished into my desk, or my backpack, or I’d leave it at home, and then it looked like I hadn’t done it at all. So, no, I don’t think this is brand new. I think it’s been there since I was a kid; it’s just become harder to work around as an adult.
Do you currently notice feeling physically restless, having trouble sitting still, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Yes, definitely. The restless part is… it’s there a lot. Even when I’m supposed to be sitting still and just listening, like in a meeting or when someone is explaining something, it feels like there’s this motor humming under my skin. Not exactly anxiety, more like my body is already trying to move on before the situation is over.

I’ll be sitting there thinking, okay, just stay put, pay attention, let them finish, but there’s this pressure to stand up, check something, click over to another screen, go solve the next problem, do something right that second. It’s not always dramatic-looking, I don’t think, but inside it feels really loud. Like being still takes active effort, and after a while I get irritated or impatient because I feel trapped in the chair.
